why: All three factual legs of the finding hold, but it is a RECORDED DECISION with a written reason plus a deliberate corporate-fork posture, and it names the wrong subsystem's file. (1) QUOTE: verbatim at auto-mode-config.md:74. The whole line is two sentences and the second does NOT reverse the conclusion - it weakens it in our favour: 'Because allow rules act as exceptions to soft block rules inside the classifier, a developer-added `allow` entry can override an organization `soft_deny` entry: the combination is additive, not a hard policy boundary.' The doc itself says wiring the user scope makes the org policy a soft boundary. (2) CODE: accurate. resolveAutoMode (managed-policy.ts:1082-1101) composes managed-then-user; the single production call site SessionManager.ts:4109 passes `{ managed: this.managedPiPolicy.autoMode }` only, and both resolveAutoModeClassifyAllShell sites (:4119, :16269) do the same. The source comments state the restriction outright ('MANAGED scope only'). managed-policy.test.ts:1033-1041 pins that the user scope composes correctly when supplied. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately: true at the Pi guardian - no user-scope autoMode reaches buildGuardianJudgeTask, whose GuardianJudgeInput.orgPolicy is documented as 'resolved from the HOST-OWNED managed policy file'. REFUTATION GROUNDS: (a) RECORDED DECISION, dated and categorized. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-managed-policy-honesty.md:207, category 'ours, stated': 'classifyAllShell is read from the MANAGED scope only, because no user autoMode scope is wired in this product and a checked-in repo must not steer the classifier band. The composer accepts a user scope and nothing supplies one.' That last clause is verbatim the fact this finding reports. The two classifyAllShell call sites it cites are additionally covered by inert-worklist §3 item 3 ('autoMode.classifyAllShell / resolveAutoModeClassifyAllShell'). (b) WRONG SUBSYSTEM, the AGENTS.md trap-4 shape. The finding says the classifier should read '~/.claude/settings.json'. In this fork that file is a CLAUDE AGENT SDK BACKEND surface (packages/shared/src/agent/claude-settings-store.ts, destination 'userSettings'), consumed by the real Claude Code subprocess via settingSources - a different subsystem from the Pi-harness guardian judge, which the autoMode wiring is gated to (`snapshot.context.provider === 'pi'` at SessionManager.ts:4108/:4119). And on THAT backend the user scope is also excluded by a separate recorded decision: options.ts:202-210 redirects CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR per-Workspace so 'a hand-written ~/.claude/settings.json stops reaching the subprocess. It is the change the isolation is FOR - a user-scope Claude settings file is a cross-Workspace policy channel'. The Claude provider is also off by default (NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE). (c) DELIBERATE PRODUCT DIFFERENCE. This is a bank fork. `autoMode` exists ONLY as a field of ManagedPiPolicyV1, parsed only from the root-owned system file (managed-policy-loader.ts:44-56: /Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json, /etc/nessy/, %ProgramData%/Nessy/, with uid==0 and (mode & 0o022)==0 enforced). Given the doc's own second sentence, wiring a user scope would let a developer's `allow` line override the bank's `soft_deny`. Our posture is strictly tighter than Claude's, which is the direction this fork takes everywhere. HONEST RESIDUALS, neither changing the verdict: (i) the finding's 'CLAIMED OUR STATE' understates the situation - it reads as if only the wiring is missing, but there is no user-scope autoMode SURFACE at all (no config key, no schema entry, no parser, no RPC, no UI; `grep -ran autoMode` over packages/ and apps/ returns ManagedPiPolicyV1 and its consumers only), so this is an absent scope by design, not an unwired parameter; (ii) the recorded reason at managed-policy-honesty.md:207 is partly mis-argued - 'a checked-in repo must not steer the classifier band' justifies excluding the PROJECT scope (which the doc also excludes, and which resolveAutoMode discards on purpose), not the USER scope, since ~/.claude/settings.json is not in the repo; the real justification is the corporate-boundary posture above; (iii) inert-worklist §3 item 3's stated reason ('the band that would honour it does not exist yet') is now STALE - the band shipped as D1 and is production-reachable at pre-tool-use.ts:2160 via SessionManager.ts:4119 -> pi-agent.ts:3835. Worth a separate housekeeping row.
correctedState: Nessy has no user-scope autoMode surface at all, by recorded decision. `autoMode` is a field of ManagedPiPolicyV1 only, parsed exclusively from the root-owned managed policy file (uid 0, mode & 0o022 == 0) at /Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json, /etc/nessy/managed-policy.json or %ProgramData%/Nessy/managed-policy.json. resolveAutoMode's `user` parameter is the shape reserved for that scope and is exercised by managed-policy.test.ts:1033-1041; its `project` parameter is accepted and discarded on purpose, which is the documented security exclusion. The single production call site (SessionManager.ts:4109) and both classifyAllShell call sites (:4119, :16269) therefore pass `managed` alone. Recorded at docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-managed-policy-honesty.md:207 as 'ours, stated' - 'no user autoMode scope is wired in this product; the composer accepts a user scope and nothing supplies one' - and, for the classifyAllShell half, at inert-worklist §3 item 3. The file the finding names, ~/.claude/settings.json, is a Claude-SDK-backend surface here (claude-settings-store.ts), not a Pi-guardian one, and the user scope is deliberately isolated there too by the per-Workspace CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR redirect (options.ts:202-210). Net effect versus Claude: the org's autoMode sets are a hard boundary in Nessy rather than the additive, developer-overridable one auto-mode-config.md:74 describes - tighter, and intentional for a bank fork.
